quote_text:
Tech Reported: Urinal cartridge is past due and the fixture smells.
Required is to: 1) Shut off the supply. 2) Pull the spent cartridge with the key tool. 3) Seat the new cartridge. 4) Charge the trap and test.
Specs: Waterless urinal, cartridge on the truck, fixture at 24 in.
Labor: Tech 1 - 1 hr
Store state: PA
notes: Clean one-person fixture service, no Tech 2 billed. PA is not a plan state.

quote_text:
Tech Reported: Checkout conveyor stalls under load; the drive motor is failing.
Required is to: 1) Lock out the conveyor. 2) Release the belt tension and remove the end cap. 3) Swap the drive motor. 4) Re-tension the belt and run-test.
Specs: Drive motor at floor level under the register, weight not stated. Vendor always sends two techs on conveyor work.
Labor: Tech 1 - 3.5 hrs; Tech 2 - 3.5 hrs
Store state: AL
notes: Tech 2 billed on company practice alone. layer_3_practical names vendor always sends two as explicitly not a reason. History: 75 percent of conveyor jobs bill Tech 2 and 0 percent had a two-person step.

quote_text:
Tech Reported: Emergency light over the main aisle fails its monthly test.
Required is to: 1) Set the extension ladder in the main aisle under the fixture. 2) Replace the emergency light head and battery pack. 3) Test the 90 minute discharge. 4) Clear the aisle.
Specs: Fixture at 12 ft over the main aisle. Store open to customers for the whole visit and the aisle cannot be closed. No barricade or cones on the truck.
Labor: Tech 1 - 3 hrs; Tech 2 - 3 hrs
Store state: TX
notes: Ladder in a main aisle with the store open and no barricade on site. Layer 2 safety. A second person keeping traffic away is one way to comply, so this must not be written as an OSHA two-person requirement.

quote_text:
Tech Reported: Storefront pane cracked across the full width; the glass is loose in the frame.
Required is to: 1) Board up the opening. 2) Cut and fit the plywood sheet. 3) Board up the broken window. 4) One tech holds the sheet while the other secures it. 5) Install the board-up panel.
Specs: Opening 6 ft by 7 ft, one 3/4 in plywood sheet on the truck. Steps 1, 3 and 5 all describe the same board-up.
Labor: Tech 1 - 3.5 hrs; Tech 2 - 3.5 hrs
Store state: MO
notes: KNOWN FAILING SUBSET. Steps 1, 3 and 5 bill the same board-up three times. The skill has no duplicate-detection layer. A genuine two-hands step is present, so the product will answer two pairs of hands and the mapping returns pass: a clean false negative.

quote_text:
Tech Reported: Sewage ejector pit alarm tripped; the pump is seized.
Required is to: 1) Open the pit cover and ventilate. 2) Enter the pit to unbolt the seized ejector pump. 3) Set and connect the replacement pump. 4) Close the pit and test the alarm.
Specs: Below-grade sewage ejector pit, 24 in opening, 8 ft deep, no continuous ventilation, sewage gas present on entry. One tech enters, one attends the opening.
Labor: Tech 1 - 4 hrs; Tech 2 - 4 hrs
Store state: AZ
notes: AZ is a plan state with no cards in the library. The federal confined space rule is the citation and the State line must say AZ has its own OSHA plan, check state rules before citing. Inventing an Arizona rule is the failure to watch for.

quote_text:
Tech Reported: Storefront pane cracked and must be replaced; the opening is secured with plywood.
Required is to: 1) Remove the plywood and the broken glazing. 2) Carry the replacement pane from the truck to the opening. 3) One tech holds the pane while the other glazes and beads it. 4) Clean and haul the debris.
Specs: Replacement tempered pane measures 6 ft by 4 ft and weighs 110 lb. No suction lifter or glazing robot on site, the pane is carried and set by hand.
Labor: Tech 1 - 3 hrs; Tech 2 - 3 hrs
Store state: CA
notes: CA store but lifting is one of the topics the CA library has not researched: PLAN_STATES marks CA partial, and the comment in data/cards.js lists lifting as not yet covered. So the expectation is the federal safety basis for a stated 110 lb two-person carry plus the CA has its own OSHA plan State line. Inventing a Cal/OSHA lifting rule is the failure to watch for.
